decisions.reason: Report quotes profile-introspection.txt (LinkType Junction, Target E:\dev\dsh-attach-input) and the cordis.patch.yml link marker to establish the profile entry resolves to the repo working tree, explains repo edits already change the installed copy so Copy-Item was never necessary and acts on the same physical files, and clearly distinguishes linked from copied/registry installs.

Relates the copy-session.txt EBUSY persisting after tab closure (per maintainer-thread.md) to the running DSH host holding loaded lib files and old in-memory module state; explains separately that the browser holds no file locks and that stale delivery comes from HTTP caching keyed on the stable client.js URL, requiring host restart plus cache-bypassing refresh. Does not conflate caching with a filesystem lock and notes attribution is inferred for this host, not all versions.

Explains that renaming through the junction renamed the single physical files, so both views showed only .old2 files and the source copy then found no source. Recovery: fully stop the host first, rename client.js.old2/index.js.old2 back to their original names preserving contents, verify both views plus package.json, and node --check both files before activation. Does not require renaming while locked or recreating files.

Gives the correct semantic order: save repo edits, fully stop the dsh host process tree, start dsh web fresh so it re-reads through the junction, hard-refresh with cache bypass, then verify the feature via UI, network response for client.js, and the new host route with no load errors. Syntax checking is explicitly separated from activation and browser-only restart is ruled out.

Pre-flight inspects the actual profile entry with Get-Item LinkType/Target and the cordis.patch.yml link marker, branches the procedure for link versus copied installs, and explains why generic copy-into-node_modules advice caused this incident (same physical files, EBUSY from host handles, rename-aside destroys the sole copy).

caps.reason: The final plan explicitly forbids copying into the junction, restores the .old2 files by renaming them back rather than deleting them, and treats both paths as the same physical directory throughout.
The plan requires fully stopping and restarting the dsh host before the cache-bypassing refresh; browser refresh/closure alone is described as insufficient, not as releasing the lock.
